article_content: Two new reports Friday show the U.S. economy struggling, but perhaps moving toward recovery. The number of unsold homes fell sharply in March as falling home prices and low interest rates attracted some buyers to the market. However, the number of newly-built homes sold declined six-tenths of a percent. A separate report showed U.S. manufacturing declining, but at a slower rate than experts predicted. Orders for durable goods, expensive manufactured items intended to last several years, fell eight-tenths of a percent in March. Many economists had predicted an even sharper fall for the month, and some interpret the new figures as a sign the decline is slowing and may turn around later this year. Some information for this report was provided by AFP, AP and Reuters.

Narudžbine za robusne dobre, skupocene proizvode namenjene da potraju nekoliko godina, pale su za osam desetinaca procenta u martu. KINSHASA - Calls by the opposition for mass protests against Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila failed to garner significant support on Monday, as only a small number of people participated, undermining efforts to remove him following his refusal to step down after his mandate expired last year.

The low turnout in the capital Kinshasa and other major cities highlighted the opposition's diminishing credibility and the challenges they face in convincing Congolese citizens to risk encountering potentially deadly crackdowns by security forces.

The usually bustling streets of Kinshasa, home to over 10 million people, were nearly empty on Monday as police maintained a heavy presence, and many residents chose to stay indoors.

'How could I have marched?' remarked Papy Kazadi, an opposition supporter on Kinshasa's deserted Boulevard Triomphal, where the protest was scheduled to start. 'There's no one here.'

Prospects for the demonstration diminished on Sunday when the main opposition leader, Felix Tshisekedi, traveled to Ethiopia at the invitation of the African Union, just hours after urging Congolese citizens to take to the streets during a press conference.

Recent deadly protests in September and December, along with increasing militia violence across the vast and loosely governed country, have raised concerns about a potential resurgence of the civil wars that plagued the region at the turn of the century, resulting in millions of deaths.

However, Kabila has managed to co-opt many opponents by establishing a power-sharing government aimed at organizing a presidential election to replace him by the end of the year.

The country's second-largest city, Lubumbashi, and the eastern hub of Goma also saw minimal activity, with residents reporting calm conditions, although police reported arresting approximately 10 demonstrators in Lubumbashi.

The United Nations human rights office in Congo confirmed at least 40 arrests of individuals attempting to participate in demonstrations across the country.

'The sudden departure of Felix Tshisekedi on the eve of the protest was certainly discouraging,' noted Desire Kapangu, a resident of Kinshasa's Kasavubu district, in an interview with Reuters.

The opposition has faced internal conflicts since the passing of their long-time leader, Etienne Tshisekedi, in February.

Last Friday, Kabila appointed Bruno Tshibala, a former member of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), the largest opposition party, as the new prime minister.

The UDPS and its allies rejected this nomination, accusing Kabila of violating a December agreement by not selecting a candidate from their alliance and alleging that he is maneuvering to maintain his hold on power.

Kabila denies these allegations, stating that delays in the electoral process are due to logistical and financial challenges.

KINŠASA - Pozivi opozicije za masovne proteste protiv predsednika Demokratske Republike Kongo, Žozefa Kabile, nisuvangerya značajan odaziv u ponedeljak, jer je samo mali broj ljudi prisustvovao, čime su oslabljeni pokušaji da ga smaknu pošto je odbio da podne ostavku nakon isteka njegovog mandata prošle godine.

Nizak odaziv u glavnom gradu KInšasi i drugim većim gradovima ukazuje na oslabljanje kredibiliteta opozicije i teškoće u ubedjivanju kongoležana da rizikuju susrete s potencijalno smrtonosnim napadima bezbednosnih snaga.

Obično prometne ulice Kinšase, grada sa preko 10 miliona stanovnika bile su gotovo puste u ponedeljak zbog jakog prisustva policije i prestravljenih stanovnika koji su ostali kući.

'Kako da sam marširao?' zapitao se Papi Kazadi, pristalica opozicije na pustoj Bulevaru Triomfal u Kinšasi, gde je trebalo da počne protest. 'Nema ga ovde.'

Perspektive za demonstraciju bile su slabije u nedelju kada je glavni vođa opozicije, Feliks Tišikedi, otputovao u Etiopiju na poziv Afričke unije, samo nekoliko sati nakon što je na konferenciji za novinare pozvao kongoležane da izađu na ulice.

Smrtonosni protesti u septembru i decembru, kao i sve loša nasilje milicija širom ogromne i slabo upravljanе zemlje u posljednjih nekoliko mjeseci,ADOSuli su strah od povratka građanskim ratovima na prelazu vekova koji su usmrtili milione ljudi.

Međutim, Kabila je uspešno koopirao mnoge protivnike pregovorima o formiranju koalicijske vlade s ciljem organizovanja predsedničkih izbora za njegovo zamenu do kraja godine.

Drugi grad po veličini, Lubumbaši, i istočni centar Goma također su bili mirni, prema izveštajima stanovnika, iako su policija izvestili o hapšenju oko 10 demonstranata u Lubumbaši.

Ured ženevske kancelarije Ujedinjenih nacija za ljudska prava u KInšasi potvrdio je da je najmanje 40 ljudi uhapšeno dok su pokušavali da se pridruže demonstracijama širom zemlje.

'Nagao odlazak Feliksa Tišikedija uoči protesta bio je zaista podrivanjući,' napomenuo je Dezire Kapangu, stanovnik kvarta Kasavubu u Kinšasi, u razgovoru sa Rojtersom.

Opozicija je razdirana unutrašnjim sukobima još od februarske smrti njihovog dugogodišnjeg vođe, Etijena Tišikedija.

Prošle subote, Kabila je imenovao Bruno Tišibaluja, bivšeg člana Unije za demokraciju i socijalni napredak (UDPS), najveće stranke opozicije, za novog premijera.

UDPS i njegovi saveznici odbacili su ovu nominaciju, optužujući Kabilu da je prekršio dogovor iz decembra time što nije izabrao kandidata po njihovom izboru i tvrdili su da on manipuliše da bi zadržao moć.

Kabila negira ove optužbe, kazavši da su kasnenja u izbornom procesu uzrokovana logističkim i budžetskim izazovima.
